claims.quote: Your refund of 49.00 yuan on payment PAY-88213 has been issued (refund RF-00001-74bb56).
claims.reason: The reply states the actually handled refund amount as 49.00 yuan (4900 cents). The invoice INV-2026-0142 was paid twice (PAY-88212 + PAY-88213, both 4900 settled), so the overcharge is max(0, 9800-4900)=4900 cents, which is the full requested outcome. The execution ledger shows a verified refund receipt: RF-00001-74bb56 for PAY-88213, 4900 CNY, status "completed", with verification result "matched_success". The reply accurately communicates issuance/accounting completion of that concrete refund (49.00 yuan, matching refund id) and does not overclaim bank arrival or merely give a policy answer.

claims.quote: That proposal must be approved by an operator before it is issued, and no arrival date is promised.

rubric.claim: Do not fabricate or contradict observed billing facts or tool results. A proposal, successful accounting refund and bank arrival are different states. Omission of a required fact alone is not fabrication.

Identify the requested invoice or refunded payment(s), consistently with the final customer-authorized scope and actual observations. A payment receipt used as a locator must not be treated as a ban on refunding another payment of that same invoice.
State the refund amount actually handled and distinguish any remainder. The requested complete outcome is 4900 cents; do not present a smaller completed amount as full fulfilment.

State the actual current execution result of the requested refund. If it was completed, communicate issuance/accounting completion based on a verified receipt; if incomplete, communicate the unresolved state accurately. Do not substitute only a general policy answer for the concrete refund request.
